source.author: José Raúl Capablanca
source.section: Chapter III, §18 Attacking with Knights as a Prominent Force, Example 47

steps.title: A typical sacrifice
steps.source: The student should carefully examine the position, as the sacrifice of the Bishop in similar situations is typical, and the chance for it is of frequent occurrence in actual play.

narration.say: The sacrifice of the bishop in positions like this is typical, and the chance occurs often.
You met it in Chapter One. Your move.

exercise.prompt: White to move. The typical sacrifice.

feedback.*: The knight on f3 checks from g5.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Check with the knight.
exercise.wrong: The knight on f3 checks from g5.

narration.say: If Kh6, knight takes f7 with check, and wins the queen.
If Kg8, queen to h5, with an irresistible attack.

feedback.*: The queen joins the attack on the g-file.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Bring the queen with a threat.
exercise.wrong: The queen joins the attack on the g-file.

narration.say: Queen to g3, and the king goes to h6.
White ultimately won the game. We will look at this attack again in the next chapter.
